Saves the app after GitHub confirms its key and installation, with its optional webhook secret stored encrypted. This is the only way to add or change the webhook secret: connect again with the key and the new secret; leaving it out saves the connection without one. Connecting also fills in webhook_events_missing from the app's subscribed events and the installation's pull_requests permission. The request must be application/json and come from an allowed origin, if any.
Removes the shared connection. The body is an empty JSON object.

Validates the saved app against GitHub and picks up its installation. The body is an empty JSON object. For an app created from the manifest without a webhook secret (created before mentions were supported), it also turns on the app's webhook pointing at POST /connectors/github/events with a newly generated secret, stored encrypted, through GitHub's app webhook configuration. GitHub's API cannot change an app's event subscriptions or permissions, so for every connection, manifest-created or manual, the check reads the app's subscribed events and the installation's permissions and sets webhook_events_missing when issue_comment or pull_request_review_comment is missing or pull_requests: write is not granted; the app's owner must then fix this in GitHub's app settings and check again. A manually connected app keeps its webhook settings; its secret changes only by connecting again.

Saves the app GitHub created from this instance's manifest, with the webhook secret GitHub returns stored encrypted. The manifest turns on the webhook pointing at POST /connectors/github/events and subscribes to issue_comment and pull_request_review_comment events. Connecting also fills in webhook_events_missing from the app's subscribed events and the installation's pull_requests permission.

No sign-in required; called by GitHub. Accepted only when X-Hub-Signature-256 matches the connection's webhook secret, computed over the raw body. A comment mentions the app when it contains @<app slug> or @<app slug>[bot], case-insensitive, as a whole word. Answers 202 with no body when the delivery was accepted and is acted on: a newly created comment (action created) mentioning the app in an issue_comment or pull_request_review_comment event on an open pull request the app opened, by an author with write access, which is then classified and handled. A clarification is answered right away from the code as last pushed, even while a fix round of the delivery is running or queued. Answers 204 with no body when a correctly signed delivery is ignored: other events, edited or deleted comments, mentions on a closed or merged pull request, and mentions that are not authorised or not on the app's pull requests. Ignored mentions are only logged on the server and not shown in any delivery. Fix requests already queued when the pull request is closed or merged still run. Answers 401 without acting on it when the delivery is unsigned or wrongly signed, or while the connection has no webhook secret. Answers 409 when the delivery (the same X-GitHub-Delivery) or its comment was already handled, such as a GitHub redelivery.

An error never fails the push or the delivery; retrying the repository stage pushes again and retries the pull request.
properties.name: pull_request_status

properties.description: The pull request opened from the pushed branch to the default branch, once it is open. A later push to the same branch keeps an open pull request and updates its description, and marks a draft ready for review when that push is verified. If the earlier pull request was closed or merged, the later push opens a new one and this field links to it. When updating it fails, this field keeps the existing pull request.
properties.name: pull_request

properties.description: Why the pull request could not be opened or updated, such as the GitHub App installation lacking the pull_requests: write permission, or a network or GitHub API error. Reported the same way whether opening or updating failed. The push and the delivery do not fail because of it; retrying the repository stage tries again. Cleared when the pull request step completes.
properties.name: pull_request_error

properties.description: Every authorised mention of the GitHub App on the delivery's pull request, oldest first, with its classification and the fix round or reply it led to.
